name: background-job-status
question: Of the jobs launched via the tracked-background-run wrapper, which are running / done / failed / stalled, and which finished but are not yet acknowledged?
cost_provenance: Reads small JSON sentinels under .claude/session-state/jobs/ and computes status/stall from timestamps. No process spawning, no network. Declared pessimistically for a handful of jobs.

args.ack: --ack <job_id|all> marks finished jobs acknowledged so they drop off the session-start enforcement line

jobs.label: string
jobs.session_id: string|null (SACT-03: the Claude session that launched the job; null for pre-SACT sentinels or jobs launched outside a session; additive v1.1.0)

schema.stall_seconds: integer (heartbeat-age threshold for the stalled flag)
schema.briefing: string (non-empty only when jobs are pending or finished-unacknowledged; surfaced as the [background-job-status] session-start line; empty suppresses the line)

fallback: Read the sentinel JSONs directly under .claude/session-state/jobs/<job_id>.json — each carries {status, exit_code, started_at, ended_at, last_heartbeat_at, log_path, cmd}. The wrapper that writes them is scripts/jobs/Invoke-TrackedRun.ps1.

provenance.authored_by: session:2026-06-24 (framework baseline staged from GitCellar tracked-background-run mechanism)
provenance.rationale: tracked-background-run mechanism. Replaces advisory CLAUDE.md prose ('arm a condition-watcher', 'monitor for stall') with a deterministic program: completion/failure/stall of long/background work is answered by reading the wrapper's terminal sentinel, never inferred from the unreliable Bash background completion notification (which never fires when the command spawns detached children). The 'every'-session + briefing-field convention makes a finished-but-unnoticed job impossible to silently miss at the next turn.
provenance.revision_1_1_0: 2026-08-03 (SACT-03, DEC-240). Sentinels gain session_id attribution (wrapper writes it env-first; null outside a session) and the oracle surfaces it per job plus an @owner tag on running jobs in the briefing. Trigger: DEFER-069 — a 41-minute Docker build was killed by invisible sibling contention and could not even be attributed afterward; and the 2026-07-30 GitCellar 30x contention pre-flight failed by hand-filtering jobs[] while the oracle's own pending/briefing fields named the peer run. Consumers MUST read summary/pending/briefing, never hand-filter jobs[]. Ack/reap stay session-scoped by discipline: acking a peer's records erases their completion signal (GitCellar lesson #41).
